nodes.name: Schedule Trigger
nodes.notes: Runs every 5 minutes. Safety net for broadcast-main.workflow.json: that workflow has no per-node error branches, so a node failure mid-pipeline (a crashed HTTP call, a Postgres timeout) leaves the claimed row stuck in 'in_progress' forever with no visibility, since the poll loop never revisits rows it isn't currently holding. This workflow finds any broadcast that has been 'in_progress' for longer than a single pipeline run could plausibly take and marks it 'failed' with a diagnosable reason, instead of leaving it silently stuck.

nodes.name: Reap Stuck Broadcasts
nodes.notes: 10 minutes is well beyond how long even a large batched broadcast should take per poll interval (25s ticks, small per-batch waits) - if a row is still 'in_progress' past that, its pipeline execution crashed or hung, not just running long. Calls reap_stuck_broadcasts() (db/migrations/012_rls_helper_functions.sql) rather than a set_config CTE — the CTE trick doesn't actually work (an unreferenced CTE never runs at all, and the planner can freely evaluate RLS's USING clause before a referenced one; confirmed by direct testing) — so RLS context-setting and the query run as sequential statements inside one PL/pgSQL function body instead, the only ordering Postgres actually guarantees. 'ALL' is used unconditionally since only one branch exists today.
